Respondent :- Asha Ram And Others Counsel for Appellant :- ,Arun Kumar Shukla Counsel for Respondent :- Nigmrndra Shukla Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
1.

Heard Sri Arun Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Nigamendra Shukla,
learned counsel appearing on behalf of claimant-respondent no.1 and perused the record.

No one is present on behalf of respondent nos. 2 and 3.
2.

This first appeal from order has been filed by the appellant against the judgement and award dated 06.02.2008 passed by Special Judge (S.C./S.T. Act)/ Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Meerut in M.A.C.P. No. 654 of 2003 (Asha Ram Vs. Shiv Charan and others) by which compensation of Rs.
2,76,500/- along with 6% interest has been awarded in favour of claimant-respondent on account of death of Sanjay aged about 31 years.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that it was a case of head on collision in between motorcycle and maruti car bearing number H.R. 26 F 8688.
The maruti car was insured with the appellant-Insurance Company.

It is further submitted that the accident was occurred on account of sole negligence of motorcyclist and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of maruti car and in any case both the vehicles were equally negligent and responsible for the accident.

The claims tribunal has erred in deciding issue no.1 holding negligence of driver of maruti car and nothing has been deducted in terms of contributory negligence of the motorcyclist.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of claimant-respondent submits that admittedly the deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle bearing registration number U.P. 12 D 1101 and motorcycle was driven by one Praveen who has lodged the first information report in police station.
Since the deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle there was no contribution of deceased towards accident.

It is further submitted that law has been settled by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei vs New India Assurance Co.Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273 that in the case of composite negligence it is open to the claimant to claim compensation either from one vehicle or from both the vehicles.

entities.text: Khenyei vs New India Assurance Co.Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. This legal position has not been disputed by learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company.
6. The claimant-respondent has also filed cross objection for enhancement of compensation which was registered as Cross Objection No.- 89 of 2021.
It is reported to be delayed by 3775 days.
The claimant-respondent has not filed any application for condonation of delay in filing cross objection.

Cross objection is dismissed as barred by time.
7.
Considered the submissions of learned counsels for the parties and persued the record.

8. Since the deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle and it was a case of composite negligence, the claims tribunal has rightly fixed the liability of Insurance Company/insurer of maruti car and there is no illegality in any manner.
9. No other ground has been pressed by learned counsel for the appellant.
10. The first appeal from order filed by appellant-Insurance Company is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
11. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, learned counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant is entitled for just compensation.
The compensation awarded by learned claims tribunal is too meager.
In the present case the accident was occurred on 20.04.2003 and the notional income of Rs. 2,000/- per month accepted by claims tribunal is in lower side.

He placed reliance on the judgement of Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Laxmi Devi & Others vs Mohammad Tabbar & Another reported in 2008 (2) T.A.C. 394 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has provided notional income of Rs. 3,000/- per month for the accident of the year 2003.

entities.text: Laxmi Devi & Others vs Mohammad Tabbar & Another reported in 2008 (2) T.A.C. 394 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The income of the deceased is accepted as Rs. 3,000/- per month.

2 12.

sentences.text:
In view of above discussion, the compensation awarded y the claims tribunal is reassessed as under-:
i.

Monthly Income = Rs.3,000/-
ii. Annual Income = Rs. 3,000 x 12 = Rs. 36,000/- iii.
Deduction towards Personal expenses (1/3) = Rs. 36,000/ - Rs. 12,000/- = Rs. 24,000/- iv.
Multiplier applicable (17) = Rs. 24,000/- x 17 = Rs. 4,08,000/- v.

Funeral expenses = Rs. 2,000/-
vi. Loss of estate = Rs. 2,500/-
vii. Total compensation = Rs. 4,08,000/- + Rs. 2,000/- + Rs. 2,500/- = Rs.
4,12,500/-
13.
The first appeal from order filed by appellant-Insurance Company is dismissed and the compensation awarded by the claims tribunal is enhanced from Rs.2,76,500/- to Rs. 4,12,500/-.

The claimant-respondent is also entitled to get interest @ 6% on the enhanced amount from the date of judgement of claims Tribunal i.e. 06.02.2008.
14.

The appellant-Insurance Company is directed to pay enhanced amount along with interest to the claimant-respondent within two months from today, failing which Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation at the rate of 10% on enhanced amount.
